Checking how `from_tuples` and `reindex` handle the mixed-length tuples in step A, I'm tracing the path through `_maybe_downcast_for_indexing`, where the ndarray-derived width truncates the tuples. The list path pads shorter tuples with NaN instead, so the two inputs behave differently in the same step.

I'm checking whether the keys of the `loc` lookup for `("a","b","c")` return the wrong match. The three-level tuple converts correctly to a MultiIndex, but the two-level engine only recodes the first two levels and silently drops the third, so the lookup matches the wrong row.

I'm weighing whether the mismatch is really two separate defects in step A: the first-tuple width truncating longer keys, and `get_indexer` accepting a target MultiIndex with more levels than the source. Both point at the same spot, the comparability check in `get_indexer`, which treats any object-dtype MultiIndex as comparable regardless of its level count.

I'm recalling how upstream `Index.get_indexer` decides whether a target is comparable, and how `_maybe_downcast_for_indexing` converts tuples to a MultiIndex.

I'm weighing whether the wrong lookup comes from the same comparability check in `get_indexer`, which accepts a target MultiIndex even when it has more levels than the source. I'm also recalling how `_recode_for_new_levels` handles a target with extra levels, and whether it guards that case.

I'm reading the upstream `from_tuples` code next and comparing its ndarray and list paths, since both get the same mixed-length tuples. The first path sizes everything from the first tuple, which explains the truncation and the IndexError, so I'm checking whether the other path behaves differently.

Checking step B now: the in-place operation computes an outer-aligned result that picks up NaN at the unmatched label, which upcasts the dtype to float64. Reindexing back to the original labels drops that label but leaves the float64 dtype in place.

Next I'm checking step B: the in-place op aligns with an outer join, so the unmatched label picks up NaN and the result is upcast, and reindexing back to the original labels doesn't undo that dtype change.

Now I'm checking whether the step B dtype upcast and the step C mask behavior come from the same alignment choice, since both involve NaN appearing where the labels don't match.

I'm checking whether the checkout's Cython sources differ from the installed build in a way that matters, since the compiled module can't be read directly. The hybrid run already reproduced all four failures using the checkout's Python code, so I'm now looking at whether the .pyx files there hold any other relevant differences.

Next I'm checking the DataFrame alignment path and the frame `&=` case, and I'm looking at how `where` decides dtype: an int block can't hold NaN, so it gets coerced to float64, while a bool block goes to object. I also want to see whether `where`'s no-op shortcut for an all-True mask skips that upcast, and whether the uint64 values near 2**63 collapse to one float64 because of rounding.

I'm weighing whether B and C really share a cause, since both introduce NaN during alignment and then trim back without restoring dtype, but they run through different helpers: `take_nd`/`maybe_promote` in B and `where`/`find_result_type` in C. D goes through `interleaved_dtype`, so it looks separate too. I'm also considering whether the one-helper, many-callers question applies to A's `tuples_to_object_array`, which seems to have a single caller in `from_tuples`.

I'm weighing whether the mixed-length failure has one root cause or two: the truncation in `tuples_to_object_array` gives a wrong two-level result, while the all-three-level case is correct in `from_tuples` but ignored by `_extract_level_codes`, which only compares the first `nlevels` levels.

I'm tracing where the truncation in `tuples_to_object_array` gets called from, and whether the same width-from-first-tuple assumption shows up anywhere else.

Now I'm weighing where the length mismatch gets caught: `tuples_to_object_array` takes its width from the first tuple, and the engine's level-code extraction only compares the first `nlevels` levels, so both places decide tuple compatibility without checking the full length.

Now I'm checking which routine makes the call that a target tuple is comparable to the MultiIndex: whether that's `_recode_for_new_levels`, which only raises when the target has more levels, and who calls it through `_extract_level_codes`.

Now I'm checking whether `_recode_for_new_levels` allows a target with more levels than the MultiIndex, and which callers reach it through `_extract_level_codes` in `Index._get_indexer` and `get_indexer_non_unique`.

whatsnew_0171_html_table.html
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.1.0.rst:170:- Added :meth:`ExtensionArray.sort` for in-place sorting of :class:`ExtensionArray` (:issue:`64977`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.1.0.rst:730:- Performance improvement in :meth:`Index.get_indexer_non_unique`, and consequently in indexing and reindexing with duplicate labels, for numeric and datetime-like dtypes, :class:`MultiIndex`, and nullable dtypes without missing values (:issue:`66125`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.1.0.rst:731:- Performance improvement in :meth:`Index.get_indexer` for large monotonic indexes, which now uses binary search instead of building a hash table when the number of targets is small (:issue:`14273`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.1.0.rst:733:- Performance improvement in :meth:`IntervalIndex.get_indexer` for monotonic non-overlapping indexes, which now uses binary search instead of the interval tree (:issue:`47614`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.1.0.rst:785:- Fixed bug in :func:`testing.assert_frame_equal`, :func:`testing.assert_index_equal`, :func:`testing.assert_series_equal` and :func:`testing.assert_extension_array_equal` where ``rtol`` and ``atol`` were applied after casting to ``float64``, so integers above ``2**53`` could compare equal while differing by more than the tolerance, or unequal while within it (:issue:`66400`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.1.0.rst:1011:- Bug in :attr:`IntervalIndex.is_overlapping` returning ``True`` for an index containing an empty interval nested inside another interval, e.g. ``IntervalIndex.from_tuples([(0, 3), (1, 1)], closed="left")``; such an index is now also usable with :meth:`IntervalIndex.get_indexer` and as ``bins`` in :func:`cut` (:issue:`68069`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.1.0.rst:1021:- Bug in :meth:`Index.get_indexer` where ``method="pad"``, ``"backfill"``, or ``"nearest"`` returned incorrect results when the target contained ``NaT`` or ``NaN`` instead of ``-1`` (:issue:`32572`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.1.0.rst:1025:- Bug in :meth:`Series.reindex`, :meth:`DataFrame.reindex`, :meth:`Index.get_indexer`, :meth:`Index.join` and :meth:`Index.difference` raising ``ValueError: Mixed timezones detected`` when an object-dtype :class:`Index` mixing :class:`datetime.date` objects with timezone-aware :class:`Timestamp` values was looked up in a :class:`DatetimeIndex` (:issue:`68577`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.1.0.rst:1047:- Bug in :meth:`Index.get_indexer_non_unique` raising ``ZeroDivisionError`` instead of returning an all-missing result when called on an empty index with a non-empty target (:issue:`54746`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.1.0.rst:1054:- Bug in :meth:`RangeIndex.get_indexer` returning spurious matches for extreme integer targets (near ``INT64_MIN`` or ``uint64`` values above ``INT64_MAX``) and failing to match genuine members of ranges spanning more than ``INT64_MAX`` (:issue:`64148`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.1.0.rst:1150:- Fixed bug in :func:`read_csv` with the ``c`` engine where a field containing a NUL byte was compared against ``na_values`` only up to that NUL, so e.g. ``"NA\x00x"`` or any field beginning with a NUL was read as ``NaN`` instead of its actual value, unlike ``engine="python"``; a column mixing such fields with numbers is consequently inferred as string rather than float (:issue:`19886`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.1.0.rst:1218:- Bug in :meth:`HDFStore.select` where a ``where`` query comparing an integer column against a value that is not a whole number (e.g. ``"col == 1.5"``) silently compared against the nearest whole number instead, so ``"col == 1.5"`` matched rows holding ``2``, ``"col > 1.5"`` skipped them, and ``"col != 1.5"`` dropped them (:issue:`68032`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.1.0.rst:1286:- Bug in :meth:`.DataFrameGroupBy.apply` with ``as_index=False`` where applying on an empty :class:`DataFrame` returned inconsistent index metadata compared to non-empty results (:issue:`48135`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.1.0.rst:1321:- :meth:`DataFrame.pivot` and :func:`pivot` now raise an informative ``KeyError`` naming the offending labels when ``index``, ``columns``, or ``values`` are not columns of the frame, instead of a cryptic ``TypeError`` (:issue:`35785`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.1.0.rst:1334:- Bug in :meth:`DataFrame.pivot_table` with ``margins=True`` raising ``TypeError`` when ``values`` has an :class:`ExtensionDtype` that cannot hold ``NA`` (e.g. :class:`IntervalDtype` with an integer subtype) and no ``columns`` were specified (:issue:`55484`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.1.0.rst:1342:- Bug in :meth:`DataFrame.unstack`, :meth:`Series.unstack`, :meth:`DataFrame.pivot`, :meth:`DataFrame.pivot_table`, and :func:`crosstab` where the ``PerformanceWarning`` about the size of the reshaped result was not raised, or reported too few cells, for a :class:`MultiIndex` with more than one level left after unstacking or with missing values in any level (:issue:`10582`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.1.0.rst:1345:- Bug in :meth:`Series.combine` using ``fill_value`` instead of the value from ``other`` when the two indexes had labels that compare equal but differ in dtype, e.g. ``True`` and ``1`` (:issue:`67446`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.1.0.rst:1349:- Fixed bug in :meth:`DataFrame.pivot_table` with ``margins=True`` and a dictionary ``aggfunc`` raising ``KeyError`` when a column in the data is missing from the dictionary (:issue:`66151`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.1.0.rst:1351:- In :func:`pivot_table`, when ``values`` is empty, the aggregation will be computed on a Series of all NA values (:issue:`46475`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.0.0.rst:260:- :meth:`DataFrame.pivot_table` and :func:`pivot_table` now allow the passing of keyword arguments to ``aggfunc`` through ``**kwargs`` (:issue:`57884`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.0.0.rst:749:- ``pd.offsets.Day(n)`` no longer compares as equal to ``pd.offsets.Hour(24*n)``
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.0.0.rst:961:- All classes inheriting from builtin ``tuple`` (including types created with :func:`collections.namedtuple`) are now hashed and compared as builtin ``tuple`` during indexing operations (:issue:`57922`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.0.0.rst:981:- Methods that can operate in-place (:meth:`~DataFrame.replace`, :meth:`~DataFrame.fillna`,
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.0.0.rst:1129:- Enforce banning of upcasting in in-place setitem-like operations; see `PDEP6 <https://pandas.pydata.org/pdeps/0006-ban-upcasting.html>`_ (:issue:`59007`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.0.0.rst:1282:- Bug in :meth:`DataFrame.pivot` and :meth:`DataFrame.set_index` raising an ``ArrowNotImplementedError`` for columns with pyarrow dictionary dtype (:issue:`53051`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.0.0.rst:1383:- Bug in :meth:`IntervalIndex.get_indexer` and :meth:`IntervalIndex.drop` when one of the sides of the index is non-unique (:issue:`52245`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.0.0.rst:1394:- Bug in :meth:`Index.get_indexer` and similar methods when ``NaN`` is located at or after position 128 (:issue:`58924`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.0.0.rst:1403:- Bug in :meth:`Index.get_indexer` not casting missing values correctly for new string datatype (:issue:`55833`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.0.0.rst:1426:- Bug in :meth:`MultiIndex.from_tuples` causing wrong output with input of type tuples having NaN values (:issue:`60695`, :issue:`60988`)
doc/source/whatsnew/v3.0.0.rst:1550:- Bug in :meth:`DataFrame.pivot_table` incorrectly subaggregating results when called without an ``index`` argument (:issue:`58722`)
